intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that intermediate junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A (JEB5A) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ITGB4 gene (147557) on chromosome 17q25.

checks.claim: Intermediate junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A (JEB5A) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ITGB4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D, that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly and underlies Non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia
checks.explanation: The title supports a homozygous ITGB4 mutation causing non-Herlitz JEB without pyloric atresia. Compound heterozygosity is not addressed in the title-only text.

checks.claim: The ITGB4 gene is located on chromosome 17q25.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The title does not give a chromosomal location.

paragraphs.text: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa-5A (JEB5A) is an autosomal recessive blistering skin disorder. Skin fragility leads to blisters that form within the lamina lucida of the dermal-epidermal basement membrane, and the disorder is linked to defects in the hemidesmosomal integrin beta-4 (ITGB4). Unlike the allelic disorder JEB5B, which is often lethal and includes pyloric atresia, JEB5A is a nonlethal, intermediate (non-Herlitz) form without pyloric atresia. Features can include generalized blistering, atrophic scarring, nail dystrophy, dental enamel defects, and alopecia.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The title reports a homozygous mutation but does not state autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: The intermediate form of junctional epidermolysis bullosa was formerly called non-Herlitz or generalized intermediate JEB. JEB caused by ITGB4 mutation is split into 2 forms: JEB5A, the intermediate form without pyloric atresia, and JEB5B, the form with pyloric atresia.

checks.claim: The intermediate form of junctional epidermolysis bullosa was formerly called non-Herlitz or generalized intermediate JEB.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The title uses the term 'Non-Herlitz' but does not discuss former nomenclature.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The title does not describe the split into JEB5A and JEB5B.

paragraphs.text: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa is genetically heterogeneous. Other forms are caused by mutations in genes encoding laminin-332 subunits (LAMA3, LAMB3, LAMC2), type XVII collagen (COL17A1), and the integrin subunits alpha-6 (ITGA6) and alpha-3 (ITGA3).

checks.claim: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous autosomal recessive blistering disorder
checks.explanation: Genetic heterogeneity is stated for EB-PA specifically, not for junctional EB in general.

paragraphs.text: Biallelic ITGB4 mutations have been reported in patients with nonlethal JEB without pyloric atresia. Missense mutations and mutations that leave some integrin beta-4 expressed have tended to cause milder, nonlethal disease. Biallelic null mutations have tended to cause the lethal form with pyloric atresia.

checks.claim: Biallelic ITGB4 mutations have been reported in patients with nonlethal junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D, that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly and underlies Non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa without pyloric atresia
checks.explanation: The title reports one homozygous (biallelic) ITGB4 mutation in non-Herlitz JEB without pyloric atresia. 'Nonlethal' is only implied, and the title covers a single report.

checks.claim: ITGB4 missense mutations and ITGB4 mutations that leave some integrin beta-4 expressed have tended to cause milder, nonlethal junctional epidermolysis bullosa.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous missense mutation in the cytoplasmic tail of beta4 integrin, G931D, that disrupts hemidesmosome assembly and underlies Non-Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa
checks.explanation: The title gives one example of a missense mutation causing a milder (non-Herlitz) form. The general trend is not stated.

checks.claim: Biallelic ITGB4 null mutations have tended to cause the lethal form of junctional epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Null mutations and the lethal form are not addressed in the title.

paragraphs.text: Across reports of ITGB4-related JEB, severity has been linked to how much integrin beta-4 protein remains. Complete absence of the protein, usually from premature termination codon mutations on both alleles, has been associated with lethal JEB with pyloric atresia. Partial expression, often with at least 1 missense or in-frame allele, has been associated with nonlethal, intermediate disease.

checks.claim: In ITGB4-related junctional epidermolysis bullosa, severity has been linked to the amount of remaining integrin beta-4 protein.
checks.evidence_quote: may enable the synthesis of some functional, albeit perturbed, beta4 polypeptide. Determination of the molecular mechanisms in these two cases increases our understanding of EB-PA and may enable correlation between genotype and phenotype.
checks.explanation: The link between residual protein and severity is only suggested, from two cases.

checks.claim: In ITGB4-related junctional epidermolysis bullosa, complete absence of integrin beta-4 protein has been associated with lethal JEB with pyloric atresia.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Not addressed in the title.

checks.claim: In ITGB4-related junctional epidermolysis bullosa, complete absence of integrin beta-4 protein usually results from premature termination codon mutations on both ITGB4 alleles.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Not addressed in the title.

checks.claim: In ITGB4-related junctional epidermolysis bullosa, partial expression of integrin beta-4 has been associated with nonlethal, intermediate disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Immunoblot analysis demonstrated a 5 kDa shorter beta4 polypeptide.
checks.explanation: Expression of a shortened beta4 protein went with a mild, nonlethal phenotype in this single patient. The abstract calls the phenotype EBS-like, not intermediate JEB, and makes no general association.

checks.claim: In ITGB4-related junctional epidermolysis bullosa, partial expression of integrin beta-4 often occurs with at least 1 missense or in-frame ITGB4 allele.
checks.evidence_quote: resulting in in-frame skipping of exon 36 and a deduced 50 amino acid deletion (1450-1499)
checks.explanation: In this patient, partial expression comes from an in-frame allele, but this is a single case and the abstract does not describe a general pattern.
